newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-Wellington's Jonas looking at S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-Wellington's Jonas looking at S.Africa.

text.p: Wellington cricketer Glenn Jonas, his province's best bowler for the last two summers, has returned home from England -- but only after a lot of coaxing.
Overlooked for the New Zealand's Emerging Players' tour to Australia late last summer, Jonas was prepared to turn his back on the game here and spend the summer in South Africa.

"I was pretty gutted when I didn't make the team for Australia, especially when I had a fairly good couple of seasons. I was lucky to get away to England a little earlier than usual and put it behind me.
"I wasn't going to come back. But with a new national coach appointed I decided to come back, basically to give it one more go.
"I had a few chats with Bob Carter (Wellington coach) and we talked about it. He convinced me to come back but it will definitely be the last year I have a go.
"If it doesn't work out I will have another season in England and one in South Africa before coming back here and getting into the 40 hours-a-week thing," Jonas said.
Jonas spent the winter playing for the St Just club in the Hibernian Cornwall league.
"We finished third overall in the league and I ended up taking the most wickets, with 73 at an average of around 13.
"I managed to talk my way up the batting order too, getting up as high as four at one stage. I scored 300-odd runs at an average of around 25."
Jonas has been included in the Wellington team to play the New Zealand Academy team in Christchurch next week.
Wellington: Roger Twose (captain), Richard Petrie, John Aiken, Ricky Bartlett, Grant Donaldson, Stephen Mather, Jason Wells, Scott Weenink, Doug Haines, Glenn Jonas, David Little, Stephen Hotter.
